generations.name: 60 Ah battery
generations.notes: Launch (I01). 60 Ah cells, 22 kWh gross / about 18.8 kWh usable. DC fast charging (CCS, up to 50 kW) was optional; 7.4 kW AC. MY2017 offered both the 60 Ah and 94 Ah packs (NRCan and EPA both rate "i3 (60 Ah)" and "i3 (94 Ah)" for 2017), so 2017 overlaps the next generation; the 2017 rows split by pack. Range-extender (REx) versions are plug-in hybrids and not part of this catalogue. Confidence: high (researched 2026-11-19, owner review pending). Sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BMW_i3 MY2017 also had a 60 Ah option; the year is filed under 94-ah (validator: no overlapping generations), and the 60 Ah powertrain carries its own pack figures.

generations.name: 94 Ah battery
generations.notes: 94 Ah cells, 33 kWh gross / about 27.2 kWh usable, same 50 kW CCS and 7.4 kW AC. The i3s (sportier, wider track) joined for MY2018 on the same pack. Confidence: high (researched 2026-11-19, owner review pending). Sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BMW_i3

generations.name: 120 Ah battery
generations.notes: 120 Ah cells, 42.2 kWh gross / about 37.9 kWh usable, 50 kW CCS, 11 kW AC in Europe (7.4 kW in North America). Sold in North America through MY2021 (production ended 2022). Confidence: high (researched 2026-11-19, owner review pending). Sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BMW_i3
